proposed_signatures.existsUnique_orthogonalHaar:
theorem existsUnique_orthogonalHaar (n : ℕ) :
    ∃! μ : Measure (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ),
      IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧ μ.IsHaarMeasure
proposed_signatures.orthogonalHaar_spec:
theorem orthogonalHaar_spec (n : ℕ) :
    IsProbabilityMeasure (orthogonalHaar n) ∧ (orthogonalHaar n).IsHaarMeasure ∧
      ∀ μ : Measure (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ),
        IsProbabilityMeasure μ → μ.IsHaarMeasure → μ = orthogonalHaar n
proposed_signatures.orthogonalHaar_map_mul_left:
theorem orthogonalHaar_map_mul_left (n : ℕ)
    (Q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :
    (orthogonalHaar n).map (fun O => Q * O) = orthogonalHaar n

exact_payload.proposed_definition:
noncomputable def orthogonalHaar (n : ℕ) :
    Measure (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :=
  Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))
exact_payload.implementation_context: Private CompactSpace instance for full orthogonal group must be constructed internally. Canonical topology is the inherited matrix subspace topology. Mathlib supplies no MeasurableSpace instance for this matrix subtype, so exact private typing definition sets it to borel of that topology, with proof of BorelSpace and second countability as displayed. These definitions are part of sealed meaning, not public assumptions. IsHaarMeasure means left invariant, finite on compact sets and positive on nonempty opens.
exact_payload.definition_discipline: Characterized source object. First compile and independently proof-review existsUnique_orthogonalHaar (real well-definedness) before writing the production orthogonalHaar definition. Then define by the actual Mathlib haarMeasure constructor normalized on the full compact group; a separately named spec/uniqueness theorem will prove the characterization. No fallback/off-source default.
exact_payload.source_range_delta: The shared background interface is valid for all natural finite n, including n0 singleton group; this is a disclosed generalization of the paper application n>=3/d>=2. It does not claim two determinant components at n0 or conditioned laws.
exact_payload.reuse_floor: No existing Samplinglib Haar/orthogonal law found. Mathlib has abstract Haar construction and uniqueness but no compactness/Haar probability instance specialized to real finite orthogonal groups. Two genuine source consumers are sign/Haar minor cancellation and Section4 eigenbasis rotation. Their different experiments retain separate adapters.

recursive_definition_audit.carrier: Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) Real represents full real finite orthogonal matrices; no determinant constraint. Mathematical correspondence to source O^T O = I uses equivalence of real square-matrix orthogonality conventions.
recursive_definition_audit.topology: Sealed inherited matrix subspace topology, with finite real matrix space viewed as Fin n -> Fin n -> Real. Canonical, not discrete or indiscrete.
recursive_definition_audit.sigma_algebra: Exact private measurableSpace definition is borel of that topology; BorelSpace proof is rfl. No arbitrary measurable-space binder.
recursive_definition_audit.second_countability: Sealed private typing definition inherits second countability through Subtype.val. Internal typing support, not a convenient new hypothesis.
recursive_definition_audit.probability: Recursive mathematical expansion of IsProbabilityMeasure mu: mu(univ)=1. This rules out zero/infinite total mass.
recursive_definition_audit.haar: Recursive mathematical expansion of mu.IsHaarMeasure, using the explicit meaning supplied in the sealed packet: left invariance under each group translation, finiteness on compact sets, and positivity on every nonempty open set. These predicates are independent of orthogonalHaar and contain no assumed target theorem.
recursive_definition_audit.normalized_constructor: Exact production proposal is Measure.haarMeasure (top : PositiveCompacts full O(n)). For a nonempty compact group, top is the entire group; normalization is on univ, not a determinant component or arbitrary local compact neighborhood.
recursive_definition_audit.no_circular_definition: The proposed constructor is the abstract Haar constructor. The preceding exists-unique theorem quantifies independent measures and does not refer to orthogonalHaar. The later spec proves characterization, and map theorem proves actual invariant law.
recursive_definition_audit.n_zero: At n=0 the carrier is the singleton empty orthogonal matrix group, nonempty via identity. Whole-group normalization and unique Haar probability remain meaningful. No two-component or determinant-half-mass claim is imported.
recursive_definition_audit.library_audit_boundary: This is a statement/meaning audit from the permitted packet and raw source only. Exact Mathlib class fields, elaboration, hidden elaborated dependencies and implementation correctness were not inspected or verified here.
